value.gap_vs_onpoint: What public evidence shows: Jumia Kenya presents a broad, price-led marketplace with local payments (M-Pesa/mobile money, Jumia Pay) and seller/API maturity via Vendor Center, but there is no publicly observable, shopper-facing try-on or fit-visualization feature. A Cloudflare CAPTCHA blocks end-to-end browsing to product pages and cart, and there is no explicit UI copy labeling any try-on as real or a generic/approximation. This creates a gap for OnPoint’s positioning: OnPoint should provide a clearly identified SKUs-based, fit-aware try-on with real stock linkage and local-pay-enabled checkout, exposed to both human shoppers and agent-facing clients via a documented supply graph and a programmable checkout surface. In addition, OnPoint should map curated African fashion categories (e.g., Ankara, Kente, Adire, Bogolan, Shweshwe) into a semantically rich, curator-led inventory graph that enables agent purchase intent with real-time stock and price signals. Evidence: landing blocker screenshot (01_jumia_landing_cloudflare_blocker_annotated.webp), try-on blocker (02_jumia_tryon_search_entry_blocked_annotated.webp), JumiaPay mobile-money guidance (03_jumia_mobile_money_checkout_annotated.webp), JumiaPay pricing language (04_jumiapay_free_pricing_annotated.webp), and mobile-app listing (05_jumia_android_app_listing_annotated.webp).

value.value_proposition: Africa''s leading online marketplace for fashion and general goods, with broad catalog, buyer protections, and local payments (M-Pesa, Jumia Pay); however, no publicly observable try-on/fit experience or SKU-level stock-visibility surfaced in the observed flow.
value.what_onpoint_should_copy: Copy should clearly bind an exact SKU/variant shown in the visual to real stock, size/color/fit context, and local payment options (e.g., M-Pesa/Jumia Pay). It should present a fit-aware try-on or trusted alternative with explicit stock availability, delivery windows, and an agent-facing API surface for real-time inventory and checkout. It should also reflect culturally-curated African fashion supply (Ankara, Kente, Adire, Bogolan, Shweshwe) via a structured supply graph that supports both human shoppers and agent purchases.
